# Hitotoki Collective

> The Hitotoki Collective ("hitotoki" — 一時 — a moment) leaves cultural traces:
> live multimedia performances of painting, music, film, photography and
> movement, staged in sacred places such as the ancient temples of Kyoto.
> The analog fruits of each performance are offered freely to the guardians of
> those places, as signposts for the forecestors who will navigate their own
> paths in their own times.

The Collective is funded by sponsors in tune with the spirit of the project;
the fruits of each performance are given, not sold. The project was born in
Switzerland, bred in Japan, and is coming of age everywhere.

The site is available in English (/en), Japanese (/ja), French (/fr),
Arabic (/ar), Spanish (/es), Chinese (/zh), Russian (/ru),
Portuguese (/pt) and Hindi (/hi).

## Pages

- [Home](/en): Overview of the Collective and its recent traces.
- [Philosophy](/en/philosophy): Why the moment is quintessential, and the
  counter-intuitive economics of offering each performance's fruits to the
  guardians of sacred places.
- [Traces](/en/performances): The archive of performances. Each trace is
  numbered and placed (e.g. 01-JP-KYO — first performance, Kyoto, Japan).
- [Trace 01-JP-KYO](/en/performances/01-jp-kyo): First performance, Kyoto.
- [Trace 02-JP-KYO](/en/performances/02-jp-kyo): Second performance, Kyoto.
- [Patronage](/en/patronage): The roles of sponsors and guardians, and how
  introductions to the Collective travel.

## Terms of art

- "Trace": a performance and what remains of it, recorded in the archive.
- "Guardians": keepers of the sacred places that host and receive each
  performance's offerings.
- "Forecestors": those who come after — future generations regarded as
  ancestors-to-be.
